thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: increased CUDA OOM rate on serving-cluster-us-west-2. Auto-created incident channel and paging the on-call. metric: cuda_oom_count spike from 0->120 in 5m.

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing alerts, attaching initial metrics.

maya (oncall): quick summary so far — multiple containers crashed with CUDA OOM on 3 nodes. interestingly, node-level free GPU headroom reported ~150-300MB when oom happens.

alex (sre): that mismatch smells like reserved/resident blocks not being available to allocator at runtime (reservation buckets still held). copying allocator logs now.

ian (runtime): adding runtime context — we've had a recent change to the reservation strategy (deferred-evict) in last deploy. could be a regresssion where reserved blocks held by evict queue aren't reclaimed in time.

maya (oncall): logs from one host (gpu-node-17):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z runtime ERROR cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z allocator WARN reserve: attempted claim 184MB, available headroom 220MB, fragmentation_score=0.83
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z cache INFO kv_cache: inflight_prefixes=42, pinned_blocks=18
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z runtime INFO fallback: selected smaller-variant v1-lite for request
```

maya (oncall): Note fragmentation_score high; pinned_blocks nonzero. headroom shows up but fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation.

lisa (platform): Can we repro with `--stress-alloc` locally? Might be workload-specific (long chat sessions ramping KV cache).

ian (runtime): good idea. repro steps I have: run serving load with long-context prompts + embeddings lookup to inflate KV cache. I'll spin a test pod with same runtime flags.

alex (sre): immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) route new traffic away from affected nodes (set routing weight 0). 2) cordon + drain guilty nodes for live reclaim/restart. 3) toggle runtime flag to allow aggressive reserve reclamation (nonbreaking env var).

maya (oncall): doing #1 now — updating routing policy to prefer us-east. will monitor error rate.

deploy-bot: Routing update applied: serving-route default -> us-east weight 80%, us-west-2 weight 20%.

maya (oncall): traffic shift applied. error rate for clients decreased from 2.3%->0.6% over last 2m. partially effective.

emily-cs: notifying impacted customers: sending note to ACME and BetaApp that small fraction of requests may have seen degraded responses, optional retry recommended.

lisa (platform): starting cordon/drain on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-19 (most OOMs). command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ian (runtime): while drains happen, I'm enabling the aggressive reclaim env: `REDWOOD_ALLOC_RECLAIM_MODE=aggressive` on a canary pod in node-18 to validate it doesn't regress perf.

alex (sre): note: when we drain, some pods will restart and rewarm caches -> short-term latency spikes. keep an eye on tail-latency.

maya (oncall): drain complete on node-17. restarted runtime process on the affected pods. post-restart, `nvidia-smi` shows memory freed and no segfaults so far.

ian (runtime): repro run with stress workload reproduced fragmentation after ~8 minutes. core issue: reserve buckets are split into many small chunks, and allocator's best-fit search fails to coalesce under concurrent pinned KV cache locks. patch idea: force coalesce on reclaim path and bump reserved-block-gc interval from 60s -> 5s as temporary fix.

lisa (platform): can we push the reclaim interval change as a runtime override? if unit tests ok we can roll to Dedicated instances quickly.

maya (oncall): customer impact: ~0.4% 5xxs across customers during peak, focused on a handful of long-context sessions. no data loss; requests can be retried.

emily-cs: customers notified; BetaApp acknowledged and asked for ETA. will follow up after remediation.

ian (runtime): patch prepared, will run CI. Plan: ship short-term flag to reduce gc interval and enable coalesce on reclaim. Long-term: improve allocator fragmentation metrics and add proactive defrag pass during low load.

alex (sre): next actions agreed: 1) keep routing weight away from us-west-2 for 30m, 2) push reclaim-interval flag to prod-canary, 3) monitor OOM metric and tail-latency. if stable for 20m, gradually restore traffic.

maya (oncall): setting incident status -> mitigated. opening follow-up postmortem ticket and tagging platform/runtime teams. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. incident severity downgraded. postmortem ticket created: PMT-2026-186.

lisa (platform): postmortem owner picked: ian. will include timeline, root cause (reservation fragmentation + delayed reclaim), customer impact and remediation plan.

maya (oncall): I'll hand back to kitchen for normal ops. closing pager.
